_comment: Lines in a tracked Dockerfile that check_docker_npm_pins.py must forgive.
Keyed '<path>:<the EXACT stripped line>'. Exact, not a substring: the two entries
below are `npm install` and `npm install --omit=dev && \`, and under substring
matching the shorter key claims both while the longer one matches nothing and gets
reported as dead scaffold. Every reason must start with BLOCKER: and say what makes
that line different -- and the gate REFUSES an entry that matches nothing, so a
stale exclusion reds instead of sitting there looking considered.
Both entries are the SAME finding in two stages of one file, and both were
established by experiment on 2026-09-04, not by reading the old comment that said
so. The experiment matters because the old comment was doubted first.

exclusions.private/account/Dockerfile:npm install: BLOCKER: npm ci genuinely refuses this lockfile, verified 2026-09-04 rather than assumed. With private/account/package-lock.json copied in AND /packages/shared present, npm ci still exits EUSAGE saying it 'can only install with an existing package-lock.json' -- a message that names the wrong subject, since the file is right there at lockfileVersion 3. It is the '../../packages/shared' key that npm cannot reconcile from /app. The registry-churn risk this gate exists for is answered the other way in this stage: npm is pinned to 12.0.2, because the crash that took this image down was node:22-alpine's bundled npm 10.9.8, not the resolution itself.
